column1: # Common Indian given names and surnames written in Devanagari (DEC-139 (d), lane C, BLD-C247): public, generic
# name lists, not records of any person, as given.txt and surnames.txt are. One name per line: the name, a tab, then
# `given`, `surname` or `stop` (a word that ends a name: postpositions, "and", the verbs that follow a name, the
# respectful "जी"). Names that are also everyday Hindi words are left out (for example विकास, आशा, किरण, कविता,
# सीमा, पूजा, दीपक, प्रकाश, आकाश, विजय, रेखा, रानी, लाल, and since the review अभिनव, नवीन, संतोष, गौरव, विशाल,
# अखिल, किशोर, विनय), as English words are left out of the Latin lists. NFC; looked up with the nukta, the joiners
# and the abbreviation sign folded out, so इरफान finds इरफ़ान.
